one_liner: C++20 YAML 1.2.2 parser/emitter whose 8-byte event tape builds about 2x faster than rapidyaml's arena tree on config-shaped YAML.
what_it_does: chyaml parses and writes YAML 1.2.2, and can emit JSON. It has three APIs: `event_parser` (pull events over borrowed or copied input), `document` (an arena DOM with lookup, path access, editing, alias resolution and 8 emit styles) and `stream_parser` (multi-document, with optional parallel parsing). It is not a drop-in for rapidyaml. The types differ (`chyaml::document`/`node`/`event` vs `ryml::Tree`/`NodeRef`), and parse calls return bool plus a `parse_error` with line and column instead of using ryml's callbacks.
how_it_is_fast: It parses in two tiers. A line-oriented fast builder accepts only a restricted subset: single-document block mappings and sequences, plain scalars, double-quoted scalars without escapes, scalar-only flow sequences, and comments. For each event it writes one 8-byte record (32-bit input offset plus 24-bit length and type bits) pointing into the borrowed input, with no copying, no unescaping and no line/column tracking; `next()` recovers line and column later with a monotonic scan. A 256-entry byte-class table sends the whole input to the complete recursive-descent parser on any tab, `& * ! { } [ ] | > '` or escaped quote. Colons are found with `memchr`, the tape is pre-reserved at input/6 records, and the DOM fast path preallocates the exact node count in an arena of 64-byte nodes, with stride hints for O(1) `at()`. It uses no SIMD, intrinsics or ISA flags.
when_to_use: One sequential pass over large, generated config or data YAML (block maps and sequences of plain scalars, simple double-quoted strings, short flow sequences) where event throughput matters more than a tree.

Tight memory budgets: the fast tape reserves about 8 bytes per 6 input bytes and borrows the input. On the author's 3-8 MiB matrix inputs it used 4-10 MiB of extra memory, against 10-150 MiB for rapidyaml trees.
You want a self-contained, MIT-licensed C++20 YAML library in two files (chyaml.cpp and chyaml.hpp) with portable scalar code and no SIMD or `-march` requirements.
Long streams of many small, plain documents, where opt-in `parallel_documents` splits the work. The README reports about 2.4x with 8 workers on a 3.95 MB stream of 20,000 documents.
when_not_to_use: YAML with anchors or aliases, tags, block scalars (`|`, `>`), single-quoted or escaped strings, tabs, flow mappings, multi-line scalars or several documents. All of these leave the fast path, and there are no published complete-path-vs-rapidyaml numbers.
You need fast random access or editing. chyaml's DOM was never benchmarked against rapidyaml's tree, and `node::find()` walks a mapping's children linearly (no key index).

Strict validation of untrusted input. From reading the source, the fast builder accepts invalid lines such as `key: a: b` and `key: "a" "b"` as scalars instead of rejecting them. The 402-case conformance run goes through `stream_parser`, which never uses the fast path, and it checks only accept/reject, not the parsed events.

Production use that needs a track record. The repo was created 2026-08-24 and has 8 commits, one author, 0 stars and no tags or releases. A rewrite of about 1,000 lines landed 2026-09-21, after the rapidyaml numbers were taken.
Inputs of 4 GiB or more: offsets are 32-bit, so they are rejected.

integration.form: static lib (CMake builds `chyaml` STATIC from chyaml.cpp and exposes `chyaml::chyaml` for add_subdirectory). You can also copy in chyaml.cpp and chyaml.hpp. A `CHYAML_SHARED` export macro exists, but the CMake file does not build a shared target.
integration.dependencies: none for YAML; links Threads::Threads (std::thread backs parallel_documents). A rapidyaml 0.16.0 source tree is needed only for the optional comparison executables.
integration.min_toolchain: C++20, CMake 3.21+. The README says it is verified with MSVC 19.44, GCC 12.2 and Apple clang 17.
integration.platforms: any (portable scalar C++20, no SIMD or ISA flags). Benchmarked on Windows x64 (Ryzen 9 9950X) and macOS on Apple M4 Max.
integration.thread_safety: not documented. From the source, all parser and document state is per instance, and the bench suite parses one `document` per thread over a shared read-only input. Sharing one document or parser across threads is not documented. `stream_parser` starts its own worker threads when `parallel_documents` is set.

gotchas: The rapidyaml comparison times only `event_parser::reset_borrowed()`, which builds the tape. It never calls `next()`, so event consumption and the line/column scan are excluded. rapidyaml's timed loop clears its tree and arena, copies the input into the arena and builds a full tree on every iteration. Both sides label MiB/s as "MB/s".

`allow_duplicate_keys = false` is ignored when input takes the fast path, because only the complete parser checks it. On the complete path the check scans the mapping once per key, so it is quadratic on wide mappings.

`*_borrowed` calls keep views into your buffer, so the buffer must stay alive and not move. Node handles must not outlive their `document`. The header says event views are valid only until the next `next()` or `clear()`.

On non-fast input, `event_parser` builds the full DOM plus a vector of event structs before returning the first event, and `stream_parser` parses every document up front, so neither one streams. `document::parse_*` keeps only the first document. The complete path does not catch `std::bad_alloc`. `parse_profile::compact` is undocumented; in the source its only effect is to skip the fast path.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick chyaml over rapidyaml (catalogued, and chyaml's own baseline) only for a sequential pass over simple config-shaped YAML where retained memory matters most. Pick rapidyaml for a mature, fast tree over full YAML. fkYAML, PipeYAML and libfyaml were measured against yaml-cpp, and yam and yeptris against libyaml, so no direct comparison with chyaml exists; chyaml's case rests on its borrowed 8-byte tape, not on a head-to-head.
verified_claims_summary: The author built both sides with MSVC 19.44 Release (/O2, LTCG on chyaml) on a Ryzen 9 9950X under Windows x64. Building chyaml's fast event tape over a 4.63 MB, 50,000-record generated file ran at about 391 MB/s, against 184 MB/s for rapidyaml 0.16.0 `parse_in_arena` into a Tree (2.13x), with 6.18 vs 81.49 MB of extra memory. An 8-shape generated matrix gave 1.16x (nested mappings) to 2.16x. These are first-party numbers from 2026-08-24, taken on code that predates the rewrite. They compare building the tape, without consuming any events, against building a full tree that includes an input copy, so treat 2x as an upper bound.
